description: Pineapple Buns, or Bo Lo Bao, are a quintessential Hong Kong bakery treat, known for their distinctive sweet, crumbly 'pineapple-skin' topping and soft, fluffy bread underneath. Despite the name, there's no actual pineapple in these delightful buns; the name refers only to the appearance of the crust. This recipe guides you through creating these iconic golden-domed pastries, perfect for breakfast or an afternoon snack with a cup of milk tea.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine bread flour, sugar, salt, milk powder, and instant yeast. Add the egg and warm milk, mixing until a shaggy dough forms. Knead on a lightly floured surface for 10-15 minutes until smooth and elastic. Incorporate the softened butter and continue kneading until the dough is smooth, pliable, and passes the windowpane test.

instructions.title: First Proofing
instructions.text: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 60-90 minutes, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Prepare the Pineapple Topping
instructions.text: While the dough proofs, cream the softened butter and granulated sugar together in a medium bowl until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg and vanilla extract until well combined. Sift in the all-purpose flour, milk powder, and baking powder, mixing until a soft, uniform dough forms. Cover and refrigerate until needed.

instructions.title: Shape the Buns and Apply Topping
instructions.text: Gently punch down the risen dough and divide it into 8 equal portions. Roll each portion into a smooth ball. Take the chilled topping dough, divide it into 8 equal portions, and flatten each portion into a disc about 3-4 inches in diameter. Carefully place a topping disc over each bread dough ball, gently pressing and shaping it to cover about two-thirds of the bun.

instructions.title: Second Proofing and Egg Wash
instructions.text: Arrange the shaped buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between them. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let them proof in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy. Just before baking, whisk the egg yolk with water for the egg wash, then gently brush the topping of each bun. You can use a knife to score a cross-hatch pattern on the topping for the classic "pineapple" look.

instructions.title: Bake the Buns
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Bake the Pineapple Buns for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and crumbly, and the buns are cooked through. Transfer to a wire rack to cool slightly before serving.

tips: For the softest dough, ensure your milk is warm (around 40°C/105°F) to activate the yeast effectively, but not too hot, which can kill it.
The 'pineapple' pattern on the topping is purely aesthetic; use a small knife to gently score a cross-hatch design after the egg wash for that classic look.

These buns are best enjoyed fresh and warm. If you have leftovers, store them in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for longer storage. Reheat gently in an oven or toaster oven.
article:
Pineapple buns, or Bo Lo Bao, are a beloved staple in Chinese bakeries worldwide, particularly in Hong Kong. These iconic buns, with their distinctive golden, crumbly top and soft, fluffy interior, are a testament to the artistry of Chinese baking. Despite their name, pineapple buns contain no actual pineapple; their moniker comes from the signature crackled, cookie-like crust that resembles the skin of a pineapple. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that irresistible aroma and taste in your own kitchen, you're in the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know to master the art of making homemade pineapple buns.

## What is Pineapple Bun (Bo Lo Bao)?

Bo Lo Bao, or Pineapple Bun, is a sweet bun famous for its unique textural contrast. It features a rich, sugary, and slightly crumbly crust that sits atop a soft, milky, and slightly sweet bread base. The crust, made from a mixture of sugar, flour, eggs, and butter, bakes into a beautiful golden-brown dome, often scored with a crosshatch pattern before baking to enhance its "pineapple" appearance.

Originating from Hong Kong, the pineapple bun is a quintessential part of the city's culinary identity, often enjoyed for breakfast or afternoon tea alongside a cup of Hong Kong-style milk tea. While traditionally unfilled, many variations now exist, including those with a slice of cold butter (Bo Lo Yau) inserted after baking, or filled with anything from char siu (BBQ pork) to custard or red bean paste. Its enduring popularity stems from its comforting familiarity and the delightful experience of biting through that crunchy crust into the pillowy soft bread beneath.

## Ingredients for Homemade Pineapple Buns

Crafting the perfect pineapple bun requires two distinct sets of ingredients: one for the soft bread dough and another for the characteristic crumbly crust. Here’s what you’ll need for a delicious Pineapple Bun Recipe:

**For the Bread Dough:**
*   **All-purpose flour:** 300g (about 2 ½ cups) – or bread flour for a chewier texture.
*   **Granulated sugar:** 40g (about 3 tbsp)
*   **Instant dry yeast:** 5g (about 1 ½ tsp)
*   **Warm milk:** 160ml (about ⅔ cup) – around 105-115°F (40-46°C).
*   **Large egg:** 1, room temperature.
*   **Unsalted butter:** 30g (about 2 tbsp), softened.
*   **Salt:** ½ tsp

**For the Crust Topping:**
*   **All-purpose flour:** 100g (about ¾ cup)
*   **Powdered sugar:** 60g (about ½ cup) – or granulated sugar, finely ground.
*   **Unsalted butter:** 60g (about ¼ cup), cold and cubed.
*   **Large egg yolk:** 1 (reserve the white for egg wash)
*   **Milk:** 1-2 tbsp (as needed for consistency)
*   **Baking powder:** ¼ tsp (optional, for a crispier crust)

**For Egg Wash:**
*   **Reserved egg white:** 1
*   **Milk or water:** 1 tbsp

## Step-by-Step Pineapple Bun Instructions

Making this Pineapple Bun Recipe from scratch is a rewarding process. Follow these steps carefully for the best results:

**Part 1: Making the Bread Dough**
1.  **Activate Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine warm milk, 1 tsp of sugar, and instant dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
2.  **Combine Ingredients:** Add the remaining sugar, egg, and salt to the yeast mixture. Mix well.
3.  **Add Flour:** Gradually add the flour, mixing until a shaggy dough forms.
4.  **Knead:** Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface or a stand mixer with a dough hook. Knead for about 5-7 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic.
5.  **Incorporate Butter:** Add the softened butter and continue kneading for another 5-10 minutes until the butter is fully incorporated and the dough is very smooth, elastic, and passes the windowpane test (you can stretch a small piece thin enough to see light through it without tearing).
6.  **First Proof:** Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 60-90 minutes, or until doubled in size.

**Part 2: Preparing the Crust Topping**
1.  **Cream Butter and Sugar:** In a medium bowl, cream together the cold cubed butter and powdered sugar until light and fluffy.
2.  **Add Egg Yolk and Milk:** Beat in the egg yolk until fully incorporated. Gradually add milk, 1 tablespoon at a time, until the mixture is smooth and spreadable but not too wet.
3.  **Add Flour:** Sift in the flour and baking powder (if using). Mix gently with a spatula or your hands until a soft, uniform dough forms. Do not overmix.
4.  **Chill:** Form the crust dough into a disc, wrap in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

**Part 3: Assembling the Buns**
1.  **Divide Dough:** Once the bread dough has doubled, punch it down gently to release air. Transfer to a lightly floured surface and divide into 8-10 equal portions (about 60-70g each). Roll each portion into a smooth ball.
2.  **Prepare Crust:** Divide the chilled crust dough into the same number of portions. Roll each crust portion into a thin, round disc, roughly 3-4 inches (7-10 cm) in diameter. You can place it between two sheets of parchment paper for easier rolling.
3.  **Assemble:** Take one bread dough ball and place it on top of a crust disc. Gently wrap the crust around the top of the bun, leaving the bottom third of the bread exposed. The crust should cover about two-thirds of the bun.
4.  **Score:** Place the assembled buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Using a sharp knife or a dough scraper, gently score a crosshatch pattern on the top of the crust, mimicking a pineapple. Be careful not to cut too deep into the bread.
5.  **Second Proof:** Cover the buns loosely with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let them rise in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.

**Part 4: Baking**
1.  **Preheat Oven:** Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
2.  **Egg Wash:** Whisk together the reserved egg white and 1 tbsp of milk or water for the egg wash. Gently brush the egg wash over the scored crust of each bun.
3.  **Bake:** Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the buns are cooked through.
4.  **Cool:** Transfer the baked pineapple buns to a wire rack to cool slightly before serving.

## Pro Tips for Perfect Bo Lo Bao

Achieving bakery-quality pineapple buns at home is entirely possible with a few insider tricks:

*   **Don't Skimp on Kneading:** Thoroughly kneading the bread dough is crucial for developing gluten, which results in that characteristic soft and airy interior. A stand mixer makes this much easier.
*   **Warmth for Proofing:** A consistent warm environment (around 80-85°F / 27-30°C) is ideal for yeast activity. If your kitchen is cold, use your oven with the light on, or a proofing box.
*   **Cold Butter for Crust:** Always use cold butter for the crust topping. This helps create a crumbly, cookie-like texture rather than a greasy one. Don't overmix the crust dough; mix just until combined.
*   **Gentle Scoring:** When scoring the crust, use a light hand. The goal is to create a pattern on the surface, not to cut deep into the bread, which could hinder its rise.
*   **Egg Wash for Shine:** An even application of egg wash not only gives the crust a beautiful golden color but also a slight sheen.
*   **The Classic Butter Slice:** For the ultimate Hong Kong experience, slice a pineapple bun open while it’s still warm and insert a thick, cold slice of unsalted butter (Bo Lo Yau). The butter will melt slightly, creating a heavenly creamy contrast.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Pineapple Buns

Your freshly baked pineapple buns are a treat in themselves, but there are many ways to enjoy them:

*   **Traditional Tea Time:** Pair them with a strong cup of Hong Kong-style milk tea or coffee for an authentic breakfast or afternoon tea experience.
*   **With Butter (Bo Lo Yau):** As mentioned, slicing a warm bun and inserting a cold slab of butter is the most iconic way to enjoy them. The salty butter melts into the sweet, soft bread and crunchy crust – pure bliss!
*   **Savory Fillings:** For a heartier meal, fill them with char siu (BBQ pork), a common variation found in bakeries.
*   **Sweet Enhancements:** Experiment with spreading a thin layer of fruit jam, custard, or even a dollop of ice cream inside for a dessert-like treat.
*   **Plain and Simple:** Sometimes, the best way to enjoy a perfectly made pineapple bun is just as it is, appreciating the harmony of its textures and flavors.

## Variations & Substitutions for Pineapple Buns

This classic Pineapple Bun Recipe is versatile, allowing for creative adaptations:

*   **Fillings:** Beyond char siu, you can fill your buns with sweet custard cream, red bean paste, shredded coconut, or even chocolate chips for a modern twist.
*   **Flour Choices:** While all-purpose flour works well, using bread flour will yield a chewier bread texture. For an even softer bun, a small percentage of cake flour can be added to the bread dough.
*   **Dairy-Free Options:** Substitute regular milk with plant-based milk (almond, soy, or oat) and use a high-quality plant-based butter for both the dough and the crust.
*   **Crust Flavorings:** Enhance the crust by adding a pinch of vanilla extract, almond extract, or a tiny bit of citrus zest for an extra layer of flavor.
*   **Gluten-Free (with caution):** While possible, using a gluten-free all-purpose flour blend will significantly change the texture of the bread dough. It will be less elastic and may not rise as much, but you can still achieve a delicious crust.
*   **Shape and Size:** Experiment with different shapes, such as oblong buns, or make mini pineapple buns for bite-sized treats.

Making pineapple buns at home is a delightful culinary adventure. While it requires a bit of time and patience, the reward of biting into a warm, homemade Bo Lo Bao with its perfect balance of sweet, crumbly crust and soft, airy bread is truly incomparable. Don't hesitate to try this Pineapple Bun Recipe; you'll be amazed at what you can create in your own kitchen!
